scenes.title: Monitoring & Operating Kafka
scenes.subtitle: Keeping a production cluster healthy
scenes.narration: Operating Kafka in production means watching the right metrics and reacting before small problems become outages.

scenes.title: Metrics That Matter Most
bullets: Consumer lag shows how far readers trail producers
Disk and network usage predict capacity limits
scenes.narration: Consumer lag, the gap between the latest offset and a consumer's position, is the single most important health signal. Under-replicated partitions warn that replicas are falling behind, threatening durability. Request latency percentiles reveal when brokers are under pressure. And disk plus network utilization help you predict when the cluster will run out of capacity, so you can scale ahead of time.

scenes.title: From Metric to Action
scenes.narration: The observability pipeline turns raw numbers into action. Brokers expose metrics over JMX. A collector such as a Prometheus exporter scrapes those metrics on an interval. Dashboards visualize trends and alerts fire when thresholds are crossed. An operator then responds by scaling brokers, reassigning partitions, or adding consumers to close lag.

scenes.title: Checking Consumer Lag
scenes.code:
# Inspect lag for a consumer group
kafka-consumer-groups.sh \
  --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 \
  --describe --group billing-service

# Columns include CURRENT-OFFSET, LOG-END-OFFSET, LAG
# Rising LAG means consumers can't keep up
scenes.narration: This command describes a consumer group and prints its lag per partition. The current offset shows where the group has read, while the log-end offset shows the newest available record. Their difference is the lag. A steadily rising lag means consumers cannot keep up, which usually calls for more consumers or faster processing.

scenes.title: Two Failure Signals
scenes.narration: Two signals demand different responses. Growing consumer lag is a consumption problem, fixed by adding consumers, increasing partitions, or speeding up processing. Under-replicated partitions are a replication problem, usually caused by an overloaded broker or slow disk, and they put durability at risk. Distinguishing them quickly is the core skill of a Kafka operator.

scenes.text: Alert on consumer lag and under-replicated partitions above all else. They are the earliest warnings of both correctness and availability problems.
scenes.narration: The operations rule is to alert on consumer lag and under-replicated partitions above all else. They are the earliest warnings of both correctness and availability problems.
